input.quote: This Agreement will automatically be renewed for periods of twelve (12) months unless either Party gives six (6) months written notice of its intent to terminate this Agreement.
input.rationale: Both term clauses auto-renew with non-renewal notice windows far beyond the fallback ceiling of 60 days: the Base Agreement § 4.0 requires six months (~180 days) notice, and SOW Attachment § 2.0 requires twelve months (~365 days) notice against a mere six-month renewal period, meaning notice must be given before the renewal even begins. Windows longer than 90 days are walk-away territory under the rule, so this fails the fallback on a material term. Redline shortens both windows to 30 days and aligns renewal periods at 12 months (preferred position); a 60-day window remains an acceptable fallback. The vendor reminder and price-uplift cap are not present, but renewals continue on the same terms and conditions, so uplift risk is limited and we note this rather than press it.

proposal.summary: Shorten non-renewal notice to 30 days and fix renewal terms at 12 months in both Base Agreement § 4.0 and SOW Attachment § 2.0
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We shortened the non-renewal notice window to thirty (30) days and set renewal periods at twelve (12) months, since our playbook does not accept exit windows beyond 60 days (six and twelve months here, the latter longer than the six-month renewal period itself). We can live with a 60-day window if you need more lead time.
